newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN EAGLE FREIGHT BRINGS GERMAN FIRM ONBOARD.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN EAGLE FREIGHT BRINGS GERMAN FIRM ONBOARD.

text.p: South African forwarding group Eagle Freight (Pty) Ltd said on Monday that it had secured German firm Thyssen Haniel Logistic GMbH as a 35 percent stakeholder.
Eagle Freight was part of South African conglomerate Malbak until it was unbundled along with two other units in December.

Current Eagle Freight management bought the firm for an undisclosed sum which the company says was over 50 million rand, but has now sold 35 percent of the group to Thyssen Haniel Logistic, which is the transport and logistics arm of conglomerate Thyssen AG
"The partnership means that Eagle Freight...will enjoy the support of a strong international group," said Eagle's managing director Bobby Pearson.
Eagle Freight has staff of 400 and operates in Johannesburg, Cape Town, Durban and Port Elizabeth.
Thyssen Haniel has a workforce of more than 7,000 in 248 offices worldwide.
